title: Generic affine-linear perturbations have full-rank Jacobian
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $0\leq c\leq N$ be integers, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Introduce $c(N+1)$ independent variables $z_{ij}$, indexed by $0\leq i\leq N$ and $1\leq j\leq c$. There exists a nonzero polynomial $H\in k[z_{ij}]$ such that the following holds. For every field extension $L/k$ (a field $L$ with a unital homomorphism $k\to L$) and every tuple $b_{ij}\in L$ with $H(b_{ij})\ne0$, put $h_j=f_j+b_{0j}+\sum_{i=1}^N b_{ij}x_i$ and $B=L[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$, using the coefficient homomorphism to regard $f_j$ as polynomials over $L$. The images in $B$ of all $c\times c$ minors of the matrix $(\partial h_j/\partial x_i)_{1\leq j\leq c,1\leq i\leq N}$ generate the unit ideal, where partial derivatives and determinants are those of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Moreover $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. When $c=0$, the single empty minor is $1$, the parameter ring is $k$, and one may take $H=1$. The zero algebra $B$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, statement and proof: exclude every rank-deficient point above the generic parameter, then shrink to a principal open. The full-rank conclusion is the rank-deficient incidence argument in that proof; the c=0 extension uses the empty Jacobian convention.

proof.text: If $c=0$, take $H=1$. The empty minor is $1$ by the determinant definition. The quotient is $L[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$, a standard smooth presentation with no equations and empty determinant $1$; standard smooth implies smooth, and the affine comparison gives the claimed smooth morphism. Henceforth $c\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, proof: rank-deficient incidence and parameter exclusion

proof.text: Put $M=c(N+1)$, $P=k[z_{ij}]$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$ and $g_j=f_j+z_{0j}+\sum_i z_{ij}x_i$. Let $\Delta_I$ run through the $c$-column minors of $J=(\partial_i f_j+z_{ij})_{j,i}$, and set $D=P[x]/(g_j,\Delta_I)$. Localize $D$ at the images of $P\setminus\{0\}$, obtaining $D_K$. Suppose $D_K\ne0$. Choose a maximal ideal and its residue field $E$. Thus the images $u_i$ of $x_i$ and $a_{ij}$ of $z_{ij}$ in $E$ satisfy all $g_j=0$ and all $\Delta_I=0$. The unital field map $K\to E$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal of a field and cannot contain $1$. Consequently the $M$ elements $a_{ij}$ are algebraically independent over $k$: a nonzero polynomial in them is a nonzero element of $P$, hence a unit of $D_K$ and of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, proof: rank-deficient incidence and parameter exclusion

proof.text: Apply the field injective-matrix lemma contrapositively to the $N\times c$ transpose of $J(u)$. Every maximal minor is zero (transposing preserves the determinant, directly by replacing the permutation with its inverse in the Leibniz formula). Thus this linear map is not injective. A difference of two vectors with the same image gives a nonzero kernel vector $\lambda$. Renumber the equations so its first entry is nonzero and divide by that entry. Then $\lambda_1=1$, and for each $1\leq i\leq N$ the kernel equation gives $a_{i1}=-\partial_i f_1(u)-\sum_{j=2}^c\lambda_j(\partial_i f_j(u)+a_{ij})$. The derivative is $\partial_i f_1$, correcting the index typo in the displayed formula of 0E7U.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, proof: rank-deficient incidence and parameter exclusion

proof.text: Let $F$ be the subfield of $E$ generated over $k$ by the $u_i$, the $\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_c$, and the $a_{ij}$ with $i\geq1,j\geq2$. There are $N+(c-1)+N(c-1)=M-1$ listed generators. The preceding identities put every $a_{i1}$ in $F$, and $g_j(u)=0$ gives $a_{0j}=-f_j(u)-\sum_i a_{ij}u_i\in F$. Let $s$ be the set of listed generators and $A=k[s]\subseteq F$. The fractions $a/b$ with $a,b\in A$, $b\ne0$, form a subfield containing $k$ and $s$, and are contained in every such subfield, so they are exactly $F$. Every $v=a/b\in F$ therefore satisfies the nonzero polynomial $bT-a\in A[T]$. Apply the algebraic-adjoin bound to get $\operatorname{trdeg}_k F\leq|s|\leq M-1$. But all $M$ elements $a_{ij}$ lie in $F$ and remain algebraically independent there: a polynomial relation in $F$ would be one in $E$. The definition of transcendence degree gives $M\leq\operatorname{trdeg}_k F$, a contradiction. Thus $D_K=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, proof: rank-deficient incidence and parameter exclusion

proof.text: Since $1/1=0$ in $D_K$, the defining equality of localized fractions gives $H\in P\setminus\{0\}$ whose image in $D$ is zero. Membership in the defining ideal means an identity $H=\sum_j A_jg_j+\sum_I C_I\Delta_I$ in $P[x]$ for polynomial coefficients $A_j,C_I$. For any $L/k$ and $b$ with $H(b)\ne0$, substitute $z_{ij}=b_{ij}$ and then pass to $B$. Derivatives commute with this coefficient substitution by their monomial formula, and determinants do so by their finite sum formula. Hence $H(b)=\sum_I\overline{C_I(b,x)}\,\overline{\Delta_I(b,x)}$ in $B$. Multiplication by the scalar inverse of $H(b)$ expresses $1$ as a linear combination of the required minors. This also holds if $B$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing, proof: rank-deficient incidence and parameter exclusion

proof.text: Write $\delta$ for any specialized minor and also its image in $B$. Its localization has presentation $B_\delta=L[x_1,\ldots,x_N,y]/(h_1,\ldots,h_c,y\delta(x)-1)$: the maps send $y$ to $\delta^{-1}$ and fractions $v/\delta^r$ to $vy^r$, respectively, and are inverse on all generators. Select the $c$ variables of the minor followed by $y$ as the first $c+1$ variables. The Jacobian block of this presentation is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}J_I&0\\ *&\delta\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, with determinant $\delta\det J_I=\delta^2$ by expansion along its last column. It is invertible because $y\delta=1$. Since $c+1\leq N+1$, this is a standard smooth presentation, even when the localization is zero. Every $B_\delta$ is therefore smooth over $L$. The minors generate the unit ideal by step 5, so smoothness on this finite principal cover gives that $L\to B$ is smooth. The affine comparison gives smoothness of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}L$.

Small cases: f=x² gives H=4z0-z1² (char≠2) and H=z1 (char 2).
